original_content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
original_content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ y=5-4t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector that is parallel to the line.
original_content.worked_solution:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ 5-4t \\ 2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}t \\ -4t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5 \\ \frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$  

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $(-2,5,\frac{1}{7})$  and is parallel to the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

corrected_content.knowledge_point: Finding a Vector Parallel To a Straight Line Given Parametrically
corrected_content.problem:
Consider the straight line given by the following parametric equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=\frac{1}{3}t-2 \\ y=5-4t \\ z=2t+\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Find a vector parallel to the line that points in the direction of increasing $t$.
corrected_content.worked_solution:
Write the position vector as

$$
\mathbf r(t)=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\5\\\frac17\end{pmatrix}
+t\begin{pmatrix}\frac13\\-4\\2\end{pmatrix}.
$$

For any positive increment $h$,

$$
\mathbf r(t+h)-\mathbf r(t)=h\begin{pmatrix}\frac13\\-4\\2\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Therefore, $\left(\frac13,-4,2\right)$ is parallel to the line and points in the direction of increasing $t$. Its negative $\left(-\frac13,4,-2\right)$ is also parallel, but points in the direction of decreasing $t$ and does not satisfy the requested orientation.
